perf.summary: Factor the Hermite basis polynomials by Horner form on the scalar coefficients to cut multiplies before the float3 SIMD combine.
perf.currentCost: Computes tt and ttt (2 mul), then each of h00,h10,h01,h11 with explicit Two*ttt, Three*tt etc. ~10 scalar muls + adds, plus 4 float3 scalar-vector muls and 3 float3 adds.
perf.proposedChange: Note h00+h01 and h10/h11 share structure. h00 = ((Two*t - Three)*tt + One) via Horner: h00 = One + tt*(Two*t - Three). h01 = -h00 + One? Actually h01 = -Two*ttt+Three*tt = -(h00 - One) = One - h00. So compute h00 once and set h01 = One - h00, removing the second cubic. Similarly h11 = ttt - tt = tt*(t - One); h10 = h11 + (t - tt) so h10 = ttt - Two*tt + t = h11 - tt + t. Reuse subexpressions to remove ~3-4 scalar muls.
perf.rationale: h01 = 1 - h00 is an exact algebraic identity (2t^3-3t^2+1 + (-2t^3+3t^2) = 1), so one cubic evaluation and a subtract replaces a full second polynomial. Fewer scalar ops shorten the dependency chain feeding the float3 FMA combine; Burst still vectorizes the final accumulate.
perf.risk: Pure float reassociation: 1 - h00 vs -Two*ttt+Three*tt are not bit-identical under IEEE rounding, so output can differ in the last ULP. Acceptable for a spline evaluator but technically not bit-exact; reject if bit-exact reproducibility is required.

perf.summary: Hoist the loop-invariant float-to-step setup and replace per-iteration (float)i * step with an additive accumulator; inline-expand Evaluate's invariant basis-independent work.
perf.currentCost: Per iteration: int->float cast of i, one mul for t, a full Evaluate call (10+ scalar muls, 4 vector muls, 3 vector adds), a math.distance (sub, dot, sqrt). The (float)i*step recompute and int conversion are redundant each loop.
perf.proposedChange: Replace `float t = (float)i * step;` with an accumulator `t += step;` initialized to step before the loop, removing the int->float conversion and using one add instead of cast+mul per iteration. Keep last t snapped to 1.0f if exactness at endpoint matters.
perf.rationale: Removes one int-to-float conversion and converts a multiply into an add on the loop's critical scalar path each iteration (sampleCount iterations). Lower-latency dependency chain for the t value feeding Evaluate.
perf.risk: Accumulating t += step drifts from i*step by accumulated rounding (~sampleCount ULPs), shifting sample positions slightly and thus the summed arc length. For a numerical-integration estimate this is within tolerance, but it is not bit-identical to the multiply form. Guard: if endpoint t must be exactly 1.0, set t = One on the final iteration.

perf.summary: Add a guard or document that sampleCount must be >= 1; division by sampleCount is unchecked.
perf.currentCost: step = One / (float)sampleCount produces +Inf/NaN for sampleCount==0 and a negative/garbage walk for negative input, with no Try* variant or documented precondition.
perf.proposedChange: Either rename to a Run-style unchecked contract documenting sampleCount>=1, or add a TryIntegrateArcLength that returns false for sampleCount<=0, consistent with the library's Run/Try* convention.
perf.rationale: Matches the stated Run/Try* API convention and makes the precondition discoverable without changing the hot-path cost of the existing method.
perf.risk: Pure API/documentation change; no behavior change for valid inputs (sampleCount>=1).
